overall: The AG found the Rochester Select Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law on any of the three alleged grounds, but recommended correcting the October 2 open-session minutes to show the correct executive session purpose.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the October 2 executive session notice was deficient because it did not list the Conservation Commission matters that were discussed.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we find the notice of the October 2 executive session sufficiently specific.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board and Town Counsel discussed the 89 Box Turtle Drive Commission matter in executive session though it was not listed in the notice.
allegations.key_passage: That Commission matters, including the 89 Box Turtle Drive Plan, were discussed during the executive session does not render the notice deficient.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board had to discuss his complaint about Town Counsel in open session at his request rather than in executive session.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, Mr. Bailey did not have the right to insist on an open session discussion of his complaint about Town Counsel.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the executive session was not within the stated Purpose 1 because no formal complaint existed, and the Board's open-session vote cited a different purpose.
allegations.key_passage: Although not accurately captured in the Open Meeting minutes, the Board clearly entered executive session for a proper purpose, and we find no violation on this point.

remedy: Amend the minutes of the October 2 meeting to accurately reflect the stated purpose for the executive session (recommendation, not a formal order).
remedy_passage: We do, however, recommend that the Board amend the minutes of its October 2 meeting to accurately reflect the stated purpose for the executive session, as discussed above.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
